intro: Lesson 32: Exothermic and endothermic reactions. To understand that reactions transfer energy to or from the surroundings

model.title: A reaction starts at 19.5 °C and ends at 26.0 °C. Find the change and classify it.

questions.model: Final minus start: 12.5 - 18.0 = -5.5. Negative: it got colder. So endothermic.

questions.q: Is burning wood exothermic or endothermic?
Name an endothermic process in living things.
Calculate the temperature change and classify each of six reactions on the data sheet.
questions.a: Answers on the sheet: for example +9 exothermic, -4 endothermic
questions.model: Teacher does the first on screen.

questions.q: Explain how a hand warmer works using 'exothermic' and 'surroundings'.
questions.a: A reaction inside gives out energy to the surroundings, warming your hands.

questions.q: Why is respiration exothermic important for warm-blooded animals?
questions.a: It releases energy that keeps body temperature at about 37 °C.

questions.q: An exothermic reaction makes the surroundings...
Big question: where does the ice pack's heat go?
questions.a: Nowhere: the pack takes energy in from its surroundings, so they feel cold.
